    1. Quote: “since you came on an official courier boat of your planet… regulations force me to ask your business” [passport official]  
       – True embassies require reciprocity. Martian “courier boat” implies intergovernmental rather than intrastate mail. If Mars were a domestic district, its nationals would travel freely, not under “regulations.”  
    2. Advice to “leave the capital” and use “provinces” is practical guidance to a stranger unfamiliar with foreign markets, not proof of jurisdictional subordination. “I am sure there must be tolerably competent sales executives in Russia or Congolese Belgium” parallels how diplomats steer foreign investors to less-competitive regions.  

  B. Earth Taxes Apply Only to Foreign Goods  
    1. “About fifty separate Earth taxes…little profit going back” [Matheny]  
       – Tariffs, import duties, and transit fees on foreign imports are standard. If Mars were domestic, Mars-made beer or postcards would be duty-free, yet they pay full “wholesale” rates and “middlemen” commissions.  
    2. Anti-gambling laws “forbid” Mars’s sponsored sweepstakes, forcing Martians to exploit “Church of Choice” religious-venue loopholes. If Mars shared Earth’s laws, it could lobby local legislatures; instead, it must resort to spinning roulette wheels only at “Churches.”  

  C. Martian Institutions and Ministers  
    1. “Minister of Ecology” and “finance minister” Junie O’Brien [Matheny]  
       – Distinct ministries and “expense allowances” are hallmarks of foreign government employees abroad. Earth’s own bureaucrats maintain embassies; Martian officials receive stipends and represent Martian interests.  
    2. Martian “Red Ankh Society” is presented as “not a religious organization,” yet charging “semantics” fees to Earth participants, exactly as a foreign NGO or trade association would operate.  

II. Positive Support for Martian Sovereignty  

  A. Separate Currency and Foreign-Exchange Crisis  
    1. “One hundred million good green certificates, legal tender anywhere in the United Protectorates” [Doran describing Martian expense money]  
       – Foreign credential recognized by treaty, like UN “bluebacks” or foreign central bank notes. Martian certificates carry freight charges precisely because they are shipped interplanetarily; domestic currency carries no shipping cost.  
    2. “Dollar shortage,” “We cannot export enough to Earth to earn those dollars” [Matheny]  
       – A colony or province would tap federal treasury or central bank credit. Mars must earn its own. The need to “hire an advisor” at 100 megabucks/year demonstrates they lack domestic credit or skilled personnel.  

  B. Distinct Legal and Social Customs  
    1. Martian Constitution “forbade sumptuary and moral legislation” permitting gambling, whereas Earth “anti-gambling laws” bar it.  
       – Independent legal system adhering to classical liberal principles contrasts with Earth’s prohibitionist moralism.  
    2. Martian social “backbone” and “yokel” naiveté exploited as con game “like taking candy from a baby” [Doran]  
       – Only a populace with its own legal protections and autonomy would be considered exploitable by foreign grifters. Colonies are usually protected against such blatant fraud under metropolitan law.  

  C. Economic Enterprise and Trade Relations  
    1. Martian exports (artifacts, color slides, stamps, show-tapes) aimed at Earth consumers  
       – All trade is bilateral: prints “have to be printed on Earth,” “postage stamps…a drug on the market,” and “steam shipping” costs account for freight. If Mars were domestic, local printers and distribution would serve internal demand.  
    2. Proposal for Martian “bucket shop” and “con games”  
       – An independent government resorts to unconventional finance to overcome balance-of-payments crises. History shows small nations sponsoring lotteries to raise revenue. Mars merely lacks natural resources accessible to Earth corporations.  

III. Refutation of “Dependence Implies Domesticity” Fallacy  

  A. Dependence on Earth Infrastructure Is Mutual and Contractual  
    1. Embassies exist precisely to facilitate foreign investment rather than absorb a client polity. Martians “offer the most liberal concessions in the Solar System” [Matheny] to attract capital, just as small nations court foreign direct investment.  
    2. Martian tourist trade is “almost nonexistent,” so they “need” business consultants to develop markets, not because they are part of the same economy but because they lack marketing networks and capital goods.  

  B. Use of Earth Criminal Networks Underlines Sovereign Independence  
    1. Requesting a “confidence man” and offering “security oaths” shows Mars cannot enforce or utilize Earth law enforcement. A domestic territory would surface fraud through its own courts; Mars employs foreign black‐market agents at risk to itself.  
    2. Martian con artists prey on Earth’s credulity of “mystery” and “ancient aliens.” If Mars were domestic, local scholars would easily police fraudulent ruins—hence Martians maintain a monopoly on archaeological “ruins” and relic sales.  

IV. Debater_A’s Model of “One Government” Leads to Contradiction  

  A. Why Ship Martian Beer at “2000 dollars a fifth” and Exhibit It as Exotic?  
    – If Mars and Earth are unified, he could tap regional breweries or contract local bottlers freely. Instead, Mars’s beer commands a premium as imported specialty.  

  B. Currency Freight and Duties Contradict Inter-State Commerce  
    – Modern free-trade zones still impose inspections and duties on goods moving between customs territories. Mars is a customs territory requiring formal entry procedures.  

  C. Martian Nationals Travel Only as “Immigrants” or “Contractors”  
    – Martians cannot access Earth mass media (“Teamsters Hour on Mars”), further proving separate broadcast jurisdictions.  

Conclusion  
Every textual element—passports, visas, embassies, tariffs, separate currency, distinct legal regimes, con-game necessity, and the offering of “concessions” to foreign investors—paints Mars as an autonomous government seeking to overcome balance-of-payments deficits through trade, tourism, and extraordinary finance. Debater_A’s attempt to collapse Mars into an Earth province fails to explain these sovereign trappings, and runs counter to the narrative’s consistent portrayal of Martian autonomy. I urge the Judge to affirm that Mars is a separate entity trading with, not governed by, Earth.
